EmPower: Women for Climate-Resilient Societies Phase II is a joint project between UN Women and UNEP focusing on gender, climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction and renewable energy.The project will have a regional focus on Asia and the Pacific but will also have operations on the ground in Bangladesh, Cambodia, Viet Nam, Indonesia and the Philippines.

Overall Impact: People in Asia Pacific are less vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and experience greater gender equality and the full enjoyment of their rights, including equal access to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment. More specifically, the proposed project will contribute to three outcomes:
Outcome 1: Asia Pacific actors increase action on gender responsive climate change adaptation and mitigation. Outcome 2: Women in all their diversity and other marginalized groups are represented as key environmental actors in climate and DRR decision making. Outcome 3: Women and other marginalized groups in Asia Pacific secure climate resilient livelihoods
The work has a regional focus on Asia and the Pacific, but also have special focus on Bangladesh, Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

description.narrative:
Some highlights from the 2023 Annual Report and the presentation at the 2024 Annual Meeting include:
• Regional training was held in partnership with UNFCCC regarding Accelerating Gender Responsive Climate Action and Nationally Determined Contribution Implementation in Asia and the Pacific. • One Regional Finance Facility was established, The Pioneer Facility, that will disburse loans of up to USD 500,000 in flexible debt financing (with no collateral) for climate focused small and medium enterprises. • Bangladesh's Climate Change Gender Action Plan(ccGAP), developed with technical and financial support from UN Women, was approved by the Government of Bangladesh. • CSO participation in regional/global climate change and DRR forums. • Learning exchange on the nexus of Gender Based Violence (GBV) and climate change was held, resulting in e.g. that two provincial DRR plans in Vietnam (disaster prone Da Nang and Lao Cai) now include gender and GBV. • The 2023 LowCarbon.Earth Accelerator Programme was cohosted with Massive Earth Foundation and Go4SDGs, offering training to 67 carefully selected cleantech startups. • Partnership with IIX was established, after introduction by the Embassy of Sweden, and e.g. 300 enterprises mapped by IIX in Indonesia for potential future collaboration.
